subject: astronomy

moments.title: Drake equation
moments.body: At a small Green Bank, West Virginia meeting (10 attendees including Carl Sagan), Drake writes down an equation estimating the number of communicating civilisations in our galaxy: N = R* × fp × ne × fl × fi × fc × L. Each term has wildly uncertain ranges. The equation organises the search rather than predicting an answer.
moments.takeaway: The Drake equation reframed alien life from a metaphysical question to an empirical (if very uncertain) one.

moments.title: Wow! signal
moments.who: Jerry Ehman, Ohio State Big Ear telescope
moments.body: On 15 August 1977, a 72-second narrowband signal at 1420 MHz (hydrogen line) is recorded. Ehman writes 'Wow!' on the printout. The signal has never been re-detected despite many attempts. Origin remains unknown.
moments.takeaway: The most provocative SETI signal in history was either a one-off natural event, an artificial signal we'll never confirm, or instrument noise.

now.title: SETI today
now.body: Breakthrough Listen (2015-) is the largest SETI program ever, scanning the nearest million stars and 100 nearest galaxies. JWST analyses exoplanet atmospheres for biosignatures (oxygen, methane, dimethyl sulfide). Mars sample return and Europa Clipper extend in-system search. No confirmed signal in 60+ years of searching.
now.open_questions: Where is everybody? (Fermi's question, 1950). If life is common, why no evidence? Hypotheses: rare Earth, great filter, dark forest, simulation.

reflection: Fermi posed his question over lunch at Los Alamos in 1950. Seventy-five years of search has produced no positive answers. The silence is itself data.
